    Calculate ADF stream apportionment for existing stream segments

    prep_adf_stream_apportionment.Rd

    Calculate static web or web-squared fractions assigning a pumping well's analytical stream depletion to a prepared stream-segment network.

    prep_adf_stream_apportionment(
  pumping_wells,
  stream_segments,
  sample_spacing,
  method = c("web_squared", "web"),
  maximum_distance = NULL
)

    Arguments

    pumping_wells

    A nonempty `sf` object with one point per pumping well. It must contain unique character `pump_id` values, hydraulic conductivity `K` with length-per-time units, aquifer thickness `D` with length units, and dimensionless drainable porosity or specific yield `V`. Geometry is transformed internally to the CRS of `stream_segments`.

    stream_segments

    A projected `sf` object returned by [prep_stream_segments()].

    sample_spacing

    A scalar `units` length giving the maximum stream length represented by an apportionment sample point.

    method

    Character string selecting `"web_squared"` or `"web"`.

    maximum_distance

    Either `NULL` or a positive scalar `units` length. Sample points farther than this distance from a pump receive zero weight.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per pump–stream-segment pair and columns `pump_id`, `reach_id`, `reach_segment_id`, `pump_to_reach_distance`, and `apportionment_fraction`. Physical segment geometry and attributes remain in `stream_segments` and are not duplicated in the returned table.

    Details

    Apportionment is static: it describes where a pump's analytical depletion is assigned, not how depletion changes through time. Use [model_adf_stream_depletion()] to combine it with pumping schedules.

    Each stream segment is represented by points spaced no farther apart than `sample_spacing`. A point representing length \(L_i\) at distance \(d_i\) from a pump receives raw weight \(L_i / d_i^p\), where \(p = 2\) for `"web_squared"` and \(p = 1\) for `"web"`. Point weights are summed by segment and normalized so each pump's segment fractions sum to one. `maximum_distance`, when supplied, excludes more distant sample points before normalization. If an eligible sample point is exactly colocated with a pump, only the eligible zero-distance points receive weight. The reported `pump_to_reach_distance` is the exact point-to-segment distance, not a sampled distance.

    See also

    [prep_stream_segments()], [model_adf_stream_depletion()]

    Examples

    stream_segments <- prep_stream_segments(
  example_stream_reaches,
  units::set_units(100, "m")
)
prep_adf_stream_apportionment(
  example_pumping_wells,
  stream_segments,
  sample_spacing = units::set_units(25, "m")
)
